- Verification scale interval: e ≥ 10 mg → {min: 10, max: null}, unit mg
- Actual scale interval: e = 10 d → value 10, unit d (scale intervals — dimensionless "d" meaning divisions). Hmm, "e = 10 d" means e equals 10 times d. So actual_scale_interval: value 10, unit "d"? Or a relation. I'll put value 10, unit_symbol "d" (divisions). Actually d is the scale interval; "e = 10d" means the verification scale interval is 10 times the actual scale interval. Canonical: actual_scale_interval_relation. I'll use label like "actual_scale_interval" with value 10 and unit "d"... Hmm. Or as string "e = 10 d". Better: value 10, unit_symbol "d". Footnote? none.
- Maximum number of scale intervals: n ≤ 10100 divisions → {min: null, max: 10100}, unit "divisions" (unitless really). value: max 10100.
- Temperature range: +10 °C / +30 °C → {min: 10, max: 30}, unit °C
- Tare: T ≤ -Max → string value "T ≤ -Max" or "negative" — it's a formula/symbol, keep as string: "-Max" with a note. I'll put tare: {value: "-Max"} meaning subtractive tare to maximum. Canonical label: tare. Value string "-Max".
- Weighing range(s): Single interval → string "Single interval". Label: weighing_ranges, value "single_interval"? Keep as string "Single interval".
- Power supply voltage: "100 - 130 V AC 50/60 Hz" and "200 - 240 V AC 50/60 Hz" — two configurations. Split: power_supply_voltage values {min:100,max:130} and {min:200,max:240} V; power_supply_frequency 50/60 Hz; power_supply_type AC. Since two voltage ranges, maybe use config_level with axis "power_supply_configuration" with conditions "100–130 V AC" and "200–240 V AC". Simpler: type_level power_supply_voltage with value as list? The rules say lists of values of Emax is model matrix; but here two voltage options are alternative configurations. I could emit type_level with value... Actually structured form requires single value or range. Two alternative ranges — best expressed as config_level entries:

characteristics.config_level:
- attribute: power_supply_voltage, axis: power_supply_configuration, values: [{condition: "AC 50/60 Hz (range 1)", value: {min:100, max:130}, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "AC 50/60 Hz (range 2)", value: {min:200, max:240}, unit_symbol: "V"}]

Hmm, or simply two type_level entries with a note. Simpler and clean: emit type_level power_supply_voltage as range? Can't pick one. I'll use config_level with conditions "Configuration 1" / "Configuration 2". Also power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz, power_supply_type: "AC".

- Software identification: "Version number: 1.xx, where xx is a number between 10 and 99" → software_identification: value "1.xx (xx = 10–99)" string. Keep as string.

Model family: The cert covers a single type "HC... Moisture Analyzer" with Max range 54–101 g — this is a range within one type, not multiple models listed. No model family needed. Actually "Type: HC..." suggests family of models HC with Max between 54 and 101 g. But no explicit models enumerated. I'll skip model_family, or include family_name "HC" — rule says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant with enumerated models. Skip it. Actually maybe include certified_type.type_designations: ["HC"] — "Type: HC... Moisture Analyzer". Type designation is "HC...". I'll list type_designations: ["HC..."] — hmm, trailing punctuation rule... The "..." indicates variable suffix. I'll use "HC" maybe. Better: "HC..." is the designation as written; the rule about trailing punctuation refers to footnote markers and periods ending sentences. I'll keep "HC..." as it conveys the wildcard. Or "HC Moisture Analyzer". I'll set type_designations: ["HC..."].

Recommendation: id "R76", edition 2006, scheme "A"? Scheme — certificate scheme A or B. R76-2006 under MAA... The certificate number R76/2006-NL1-15.39. Scheme: not explicitly stated in markdown. OIML-CS certificates have scheme A or B. Not stated — omit. Hmm, rule: scheme (A|B) in certificate. Since not present, omit or null. I'll omit.

Accuracy classes: ["II"] — the Ⅱ is Roman numeral two (U+2161). Use "II".

Test reports: id "NMi-15200443-01", date "2015-08-20", pages 51, role "test_report". Actually OIML Test Report — role could be type_evaluation_report. The doc says "associated OIML Test Report(s)". Role: "test_report" seems fine; schema says role: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. Choose "test_report".
